At step 19 (pass, the end step) gorge has stack [ability:Ghost of Illyria@p0], Forge has the same ability at checkpoints step 19 and step 20, and XMage has stack []. CR 603.7a: "Delayed triggered abilities are created during the resolution of spells or abilities, as the result of a replacement effect being applied, or as a result of a static ability that allows a player to take an action. A delayed triggered ability won't trigger until it has actually been created, even if its trigger event occurred just beforehand." CR 115.6: a spell or ability that allows zero targets to be chosen "is still said to require targets, but that spell or ability is targeted only if one or more targets have been chosen for it"; the ability resolves and creates the delayed return ability, which then resolves doing nothing (CR 603.7e makes its source Ghost of Illyria, as gorge and Forge show). XMage's ExileReturnBattlefieldNextEndStepTargetEffect.apply returns false at lines 78-80 when toExile is empty, before game.addDelayedTriggeredAbility at line 86, so the trigger is never created; GhostOfIllyria.java:45-46 uses that effect with new TargetPermanent(0, 1, filter). Forge's script always runs SubAbility$ DelTrig (ghost_of_illyria.txt:7-8 with TargetMin$ 0), and XMage's own PheliaExuberantShepherd.java:94 notes "delayed trigger is created even if exiling failed." Verdict (b) XMage: create the delayed trigger even when toExile is empty (the shared effect, so the other optional-target users are covered too); branch fix/ghost-of-illyria-delayed-trigger commit 917dc13a936b76e3dc2f425f5995746024d7626e, PR adams-shaun/mage#1; the farm's XMAGE_REF 4142596fb7 predates the fix. Not a harness divergence: the engines agree at every other checkpoint and the difference is this effect returning early.
